questions.statement: Which thing do you send to invite friends to your birthday party?
questions.context: In a house in Bogotá, a girl writes birthday cards for her party on Saturday.

options.feedback: Homework is school work, not for inviting friends.
A thermometer measures temperature, not for invitations.
Invitation card is correct because it invites friends to the party.
An umbrella protects from rain, not for inviting friends.

questions.explanation: La palabra invitation es clave para organizar fiestas. También se combina con send an invitation y birthday card.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Invitation: Come to my party on Sunday at 4:00. What day is the party?
questions.context: In a school in Medellín, a boy reads an invitation for a party on Sunday afternoon.

options.feedback: On Sunday is correct because the invitation says Sunday.
On Monday is a different day, not Sunday.
On Friday is a different day, not Sunday.
On Tuesday is a different day, not Sunday.

questions.explanation: La comprensión lectora localiza el día dentro de la invitación. Además, la preposición on acompaña días de la semana.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Would you like to come to my party? Yes, ___. Which answer accepts the invitation politely?
questions.context: In a park in Cali, a girl invites her friend to her birthday party with cake.

options.feedback: This answer declines rudely and does not accept.
Maybe rain is wet does not answer the invitation.
Sorry I cannot go declines the invitation, not accepts.
I would love to come is correct because it accepts politely.

questions.explanation: La respuesta I would love to acepta con entusiasmo y cortesía. También contrasta con Sorry, I cannot, que rechaza la invitación.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Can you come to my party on Saturday? Sorry, I ___ come. I visit my grandmother. Which verb declines politely?
questions.context: In a house in Bucaramanga, a boy declines an invitation because he visits his grandmother.

options.feedback: Can party happy is not correct grammar for declining.
Cannot is correct because it politely declines with sorry.
Love to party accepts, it does not decline the invitation.
Am cake is incorrect grammar and unrelated to invitations.

questions.explanation: La forma sorry más cannot rechaza con educación. Es importante añadir el motivo para mantener la cortesía.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: At a birthday party, you can see balloons, cake and ___. Which word belongs to a party?
questions.context: At a birthday party in Pereira, children eat cake and receive balloons and gifts.

options.feedback: Exams are school tests, not party objects.
Gifts is correct because birthday parties have gifts.
Toothaches are pains, not party objects.
Buses are transport, not typical party objects.

questions.explanation: El vocabulario balloon, cake y gift describe una fiesta típica. También es útil usarlos para elaborar una lista de la fiesta.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Invite 1: Party on Friday at 5:00. Invite 2: Party on Saturday at 3:00. Luisa can go on Saturday. Which party can Luisa join?
questions.context: In a classroom in Cartagena, Luisa reads two invitations with different dates and times.

options.text: Invite 2, because it is on Saturday at 3:00.
options.feedback: Invite 2 is correct because it matches her free day.

options.text: Invite 1, because it is on Saturday too.
options.feedback: Invite 1 is on Friday, not on Saturday.

options.text: Both, because Friday and Saturday are the same day.
options.feedback: Friday and Saturday are different days.

options.text: Neither, because parties are on Monday.
options.feedback: The invitations say Friday and Saturday, not Monday.

questions.explanation: Analizar exige comparar día y hora con la disponibilidad. Además, es clave distinguir Friday de Saturday en la invitación.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Answer 1: Sure, I would love to come. Answer 2: No, your party is boring. Which answer is polite?
questions.context: In a school in Manizales, a teacher shows polite and rude answers to an invitation.

options.feedback: Boring is rude and hurts feelings.

options.text: Both, because both accept the invitation.
options.feedback: Answer 2 does not accept, it rejects rudely.

options.text: Neither, because invitations need no answer.
options.feedback: Invitations need a polite accept or decline answer.

options.text: Answer 1, because sure and love show enthusiasm.
options.feedback: Answer 1 is correct because it accepts with kind words.

questions.explanation: Distinguir el tono cortés del grosero es esencial en comunicación. También el uso de sure y love suaviza la respuesta.
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Card 1: Party on Sunday at 4:00, address included. Card 2: Party, no day, no time. Card 3: Party on Monday at 9:00 in the morning during school. Which is the best invitation?
questions.context: In a stationery shop in Santa Marta, a boy evaluates three invitation cards before buying one.

options.text: Card 2, because missing information is clear.
options.feedback: Missing day and time makes the invitation unclear.

options.text: Card 1, because it has day, time and address clearly.
options.feedback: This is correct because a good invitation needs day, time and place.

options.text: Card 3, because school time is perfect for a party.
options.feedback: A party during school hours is not convenient.
Only Card 1 has complete and convenient information.

questions.explanation: Evaluar una invitación exige verificar día, hora y lugar. Asimismo, una buena invitación evita horarios imposibles como la jornada escolar.
questions.subject: ingles
